What is the difference in using local or web claude session?

It comes down to where I run and which files I can see.

**Local session (what you're using now: Claude Code in VS Code)**
- I run on your computer, in WSL, so I see your files exactly as they are right now, including work you haven't committed. That's how I could review your `index.html` before you committed it.
- Commands I run (`git status`, `ls`, a local server) run on your machine.
- My memory notes (your profile, the plan, "teach, don't build") are saved on your machine, so they carry over between local sessions.

**Web session (claude.ai/code)**
- I run in a temporary cloud machine that clones your repo from GitHub. So your code has to be pushed to GitHub first.
- I only see what you've pushed. Uncommitted or unpushed work on your PC is invisible to me.
- Changes I make end up on a branch on GitHub, and you pull them to get them locally.
- It's handy for longer tasks running in the background, or for working from another computer or your phone.
- My local memory notes aren't there, so I wouldn't remember your plan or how you want to learn.

**Plain claude.ai chat (no Code)**
- It can't see your repo at all. You'd have to paste your code in.

**For GameLife, stay local.** You're learning, so you want me reading your work in progress, reviewing before commits, and keeping our notes between sessions. A web session only starts making sense once your repo is on GitHub, which comes later in the plan anyway (hosting on GitHub Pages).
